pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: auth-probe-odd-ips triggered (sev: high) — paging sam (oncall)

sam (oncall): taking it 

sam (oncall): seeing ~500 401s to /auth/introspect from 18.205.93.0/24 hitting staging front door. short spike ~2m ago.

leah (sec-eng): I pulled the logs — some requests include an Authorization header fragment. Also found an S3 object with a token snippet: `s3://redwood-staging-logs/2026-03-18/events.log` contains 'Bearer sk-infra-ingest-7a3f...'.

carlos (sre): is that a prod key or staging-only?

sam (oncall): bucket is staging but the token maps to service account `ingest-writer` (used by infra pipelines). Last rotation timestamp looks like 72h ago. not sure if fully live.

tori (support): any customer traffic impacted?

sam (oncall): route analysis shows requests with test-tenant ids only, no paid-customer proxied traffic observed. still treat as P1 because creds are present in logs.

leah (sec-eng): immediate containment plan: 1) block offending CIDR at edge (WAF/ipset) 2) revoke ingest-writer token 3) quarantine the S3 object (make read-only snapshot, remove public ACLs) 4) preserve copies for forensics.

sam (oncall): applying mitigations now. pushing WAF rule and preparing revocation.

sam (oncall): commands I'm running:
```
infractl waf block --cidr 18.205.93.0/24 --reason "suspicious auth probes"
infractl iam revoke-key --service ingest-writer --force
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-staging-logs/2026-03-18/events.log /tmp/forensics/events.log
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-staging-logs/2026-03-18/events.log s3://redwood-incidents-archive/IR-3259876543/ --acl private
```

ops-bot: WAF rule wf-998 applied to staging-lb (edge) — blocking 18.205.93.0/24.

carlos (sre): I'll run an account-wide grep for token patterns across buckets and lock down staging-logs ACLs. running: `aws s3api list-objects --bucket redwood-staging-logs | xargs -n1 -I{} aws s3 cp s3://redwood-staging-logs/{} /tmp/scan/`

leah (sec-eng): @legal-oncall please standby — we may need privacy/legal notification depending on extent. Also enable S3 access logs and increase retention for the incident archive.

tori (support): I'll draft a short internal update and a customer-safe template in case we need to escalate. won't send until we confirm prod tokens unaffected.

sam (oncall): mitigations done: WAF wf-998 up, revoke call returned `revoke-id:r-3345` for ingest-writer. archived the suspect object to incidents bucket. initial grep across prod buckets returned 0 matches for 'sk-infra-ingest' prefix.

leah (sec-eng): good. next steps: rotate the ingest-writer service account credentials, audit CI/CD pipelines for any accidental secret checkins (search recent merges for 'ingest-writer' or token fragments), preserve forensic copies, and open an incident runbook link.

sam (oncall): opened incident doc at https://incidents.redwood.ai/IR-3259876543 — added timeline + artifacts.

carlos (sre): scheduled rotation job for 10:05 UTC (rotation-job-325987) and will post result here.

legal-oncall: pinged — will join if we need to prepare an external notice.

leah (sec-eng): containment verified :white_check_mark: scanning for lateral leaks (CI, deploy logs, S3) in progress. mark state = CONTAINMENT.

tori (support): draft ready, standing by for 'customer-impact: yes' decision.

sam (oncall): closing the pager for now — watchlist on the IP and service account. will escalate if we see further auth attempts or new token sightings.

leah (sec-eng): nice quick work. keep the incident open until key rotation + CI audit complete.

sam (oncall): will update incident doc with final remediation steps and timeline once rotation completes.
